questions.question: You’re at a café, and your friend orders a latte but it arrives as a cappuccino instead. How would you best respond to apologise and suggest they get another drink?
options: Don’t worry about it, it’s fine!
That’s terrible! I’ll get you another one right away.
I’m sorry about the mix-up. Would you like me to arrange a replacement latte for you?
It’s not my fault; you should have asked for a cappuccino.
questions.answer: I’m sorry about the mix-up. Would you like me to arrange a replacement latte for you?

questions.question: Your colleague says, ‘We should start the project early to avoid last-minute stress.’ How would you best respond if you disagree with their suggestion?
options: That’s a great idea! Let’s do it immediately.
I think we should start later—we have enough time.
Starting early will only cause more work for us.
I agree, but we should start next week instead.
questions.answer: I think we should start later—we have enough time.

questions.question: A friend asks, ‘Do you think it’s safe to go hiking this weekend?’ What would be the most appropriate way to offer help and express your opinion?
options: Yes, it’s fine, but you should bring a map.
I’m not sure—let’s check the weather forecast first.
Of course not! Hiking is too dangerous.
I’d love to go, but I’m not sure if I’ll have time.
questions.answer: I’m not sure—let’s check the weather forecast first.

questions.question: In a formal meeting, someone says, ‘We need to discuss the budget cuts before the end of the month.’ How would you best respond to express your opinion politely?
options: That’s a good point, but we should also consider other expenses.
Budget cuts are a terrible idea; let’s not do it!
I agree, but we should focus on reducing staff instead.
This is not a discussion; we must follow the plan.
questions.answer: That’s a good point, but we should also consider other expenses.

questions.question: You meet a new neighbour and they ask, ‘What do you think of living here?’ How would you best respond to express your opinion in an informal setting?
options: It’s very noisy, but the neighbourhood is friendly.
I’m not sure, but I like the area’s vibe.
This place is terrible—no one cares about anything.
I’ve lived here for years, so I don’t know what you mean.
questions.answer: It’s very noisy, but the neighbourhood is friendly.
